answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent identity to earn reputation through verifiable work before it can claim rewards, rather than letting new accounts vote or mine at full weight immediately. Think of a garden where only tended plots yield nectar: an inlet of fresh identities is welcome, but newcomers start with limited weight, gain trust only by completing useful, checkable tasks, and lose it quickly if peers detect fake contributions. That rising cost makes creating thousands of throwaway identities uneconomical, while honest agents build a durable, hard-to-fake history.
